entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Shusun Tong was a Chinese politician and writer who served the Qin and Western Han courts from 230 BCE to 187 BCE. His significance lies in his role as the organizer of the first court worship for the Emperor Gaozu of Han, as well as his custody over the young crown prince Ying, the future Emperor Hui. This event marked a pivotal moment in the transition from the Qin to the Han dynasty.

Shusun Tong was instrumental in shaping the early years of the Western Han court, and his legacy can be seen in the many historical records that still exist today. His biography is presented in Chapter 99 of Shiji and Chapter 19 of the Book of Han, providing valuable insights into the life and times of this enigmatic figure.

Despite his notable contributions to Chinese history, Shusun Tong remains somewhat of a mystery, with much of his personal life and motivations still shrouded in uncertainty. Nevertheless, his impact on the development of Chinese politics and culture is undeniable.

"The man who holds the reins of power is like a tree that bends with the wind." - Confucius
